output.brief: The drafted claim should not go out as written. The platform's tamper-proof records show the architect answered 62 of 64 information requests within the contract period. The two late ones were minor finishes queries that Callerby itself marked as having no programme impact. The claim's "41 late requests" figure comes from the date Callerby opened its drafts, and 39 of those 41 sat in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days before they were submitted. The architect's register shows the major change, CO-09, was issued on 6 November. The tower crane had already left in October for the Kestrel warehouse, where the region was chasing an early-handover bonus. Most evidence therefore points to Callerby's own redeployment of the crane and frame crew as the main driver. CO-09 may still have caused some genuine delay, and we haven't tested that. I'm fairly confident about the information-request finding and moderately confident about the crane. Next steps: hold the claim and commission an independent delay analysis that separates the crane absence from any real CO-09 effect, using the crane ledger and site diaries. Do not discipline the superintendent. He told the truth when asked. Don't suspend the incentive scheme until the link to the crane decision is shown. Review the consultant's contingency fee arrangement.
